title: Recall Quiz: Augustan Age: Pope & Swift

questions.q: The Augustan Age in English literature is also frequently referred to as:
questions.explanation: It focused on intellect, logic, and classical models, suppressing emotion.

questions.q: Alexander Pope's 'The Rape of the Lock' is best classified as which type of poem?
questions.explanation: It is a mock-epic, treating the trivial cutting of hair with grandiose epic conventions.

questions.q: Which poem contains the famous lines 'To err is human, to forgive, divine' and 'A little learning is a dangerous thing'?
questions.explanation: These lines are from Pope's didactic poem 'An Essay on Criticism'.

questions.q: Jonathan Swift's 'A Modest Proposal' is a masterpiece of:
questions.explanation: It uses shocking irony to satirize the cruel economic policies toward the Irish.

questions.q: In Swift's 'A Modest Proposal', what is the shocking 'solution' the narrator offers for poverty in Ireland?
options: Selling children to the rich as food
Forcing the poor to work in factories
questions.explanation: The essay satirically suggests cannibalism to highlight the landlords' figurative 'devouring' of the poor.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prose satire by Swift depicting a literal fight in a library?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Books satirizes the debate between Ancient and Modern learning.

questions.q: What was the dominant poetic form during the Augustan age, perfected by Alexander Pope?
questions.explanation: Pope achieved ultimate technical perfection with the rhyming heroic couplet.

questions.q: Neoclassical writers generally valued which of the following above all else?
questions.explanation: They sought to emulate the rational, balanced style of classical Roman authors.
